summary: Iteration 3: tested the WhatsApp floating button, Contact page Google Map, customer thank-you email and the enquiry/contact regression. Everything requested passed. Backend: 14/14 pytest passed, including the earlier rule tests. The customer email was confirmed in the backend log: an enquiry with an email gave 2 email sends (admin + customer), both 202 Accepted, and the API answered in under 3s. Phone-only gave 1 send (admin) with no errors. Frontend: the WhatsApp button shows on /, /digital-marketing, /it-products and /contact at 1280 and 390. It has the correct wa.me/919692791725 link with the encoded 'Hi XOLNET Technologies' message and target=_blank. On mobile it shows the icon only (56x56, bottom-right) and does not cover CTAs. The enquiry modal overlay (z-50) correctly sits above it. The map iframe and directions link are correct and lay out well at both widths. The contact form and the multi-step modal submit successfully, and the phone-or-email toast is enforced.

minor.issue: When submissions come in a burst, the Emergent email provider returns 429 rate_limited. send_email only logs a warning, with no retry or queue, so those admin/customer emails are silently lost (seen at 12:02 during parallel test runs). Normal single submissions work (202).

action_items: Optional: add a simple retry/backoff on 429 in send_email, or persist an email_status field on the enquiry so lost notifications are visible in the admin panel
critical_code_review_comments: asyncio.create_task results are not stored. Keep references in a set (and discard them on done) so tasks can't be garbage-collected mid-flight
_assert_safe_email is called outside the try block in send_email. A ValueError would surface as an unretrieved task exception instead of a logged error
server.py is ~518 lines; it is getting close to the point where email helpers/templates should move into their own module
seed_data_creation: TEST_ leads were created and then deleted via mongo cleanup in test_cleanup
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run the email-count test with '-n 0' (pytest.ini uses xdist). Avoid running it in parallel with other enquiry tests: the email provider rate-limits bursts (429) and other tests add sends. Assert '202 Accepted', not '202' (the log dates contain 2026). The preview URL sometimes shows a Cloudflare challenge page; just retry.
